We train a T5-Base model on HotpotQA ... to generate questions for our conversational chunks. ... We train a BART summarizer on News and dialogue summarization corpora and run QG models on top of the generated summaries.
We train a multi-hop question generator and a dialogue summarizer to generate QA pairs.

We follow the standard evaluation metrics in the QA community: exact match (EM) and F1 scores. The EM score is a strict score that predicted answers have to be the same as the ground truth answers. The F1 score is calculated by tokens overlapping between predicted answers and ground truth answers. In addition, we also report the FZ-R scores, which used the Levenshtein distance to calculate the differences between sequences.

We ask three annotators to first write an answer to the given question and conversation, then label fluency (how fluent and grammatically correct the question is, from 0 to 2), complexity (how hard to find an answer, from 0 to 2), and confidence (whether they are confident with their answer, 0 or 1).

guideline: Annotators evaluate questions based on fluency, complexity, and confidence.
Rate fluency of the question, complexity of finding the answer, and confidence of the answer.

Rate [Fluency of the question]: (A) The question is fluent and has good grammar. I can understand clearly. (B) The question is somewhat fluent with some minor grammar errors. But it does not influence my reading. (C) The question is not fluent and has serious grammar error. I can hardly understand it. Rate [Complexity of the question]: (A) The answer to the question is hard to find. I have to read the whole conversation back-and-forth more than one time. (B) The answer to the question is not that hard to find. I can find the answer by reading several sentences once. (C) The answer to the question is easy to find. I can find the answer by only reading only one sentence. Rate [Confidence of the answer]: (A) I am confident that my answer is correct. (B) I am not confident that my answer is correct.
